title: test(cli): production-posture spawns take a kernel-assigned port; a pin holds every bin/run.js spawner to it
body:
Fixes #24295

Clause-②: no

Basis for the Clause-② line: every changed file is under `packages/cli/test/**`, the CLI's test harness. `@objectstack/cli` publishes `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` (its `files[]`). Measured after the build: the new symbols (`KERNEL_ASSIGNED_PORT`, `readKernelAssignedPort`, `OUTSIDE_THE_PRODUCTION_COLUMN`) occur in 0 of those files. The positive control `childPortEnv`, which comes from `src/`, occurs in 2. Nothing published moves, so this PR carries the `skip-changeset` label and no changeset. This repo refuses a new empty-frontmatter changeset (`scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`, rule 1), so an empty changeset was not an option.

## What changed

- **The closed mechanism** (`test/helpers/serve-process.ts`): `KERNEL_ASSIGNED_PORT` (`'0'`) and `readKernelAssignedPort(output, what)`.
  - A production-posture spawn passes `--port 0`. Its own kernel picks the port when it binds, so no released number sits in a gap.
  - The test reads the bound port back from the banner tail.
  - `readKernelAssignedPort` returns an `Error` for three cases: no banner, an unreadable `API:` row, or `localhost:0` announced.
- **Every production-posture spawn site** now uses that mechanism (9 files). Two sites needed a number before the spawn (A3). For them, the number the test needs is a `holdPort()` held for the whole boot, so the child never binds it.
- **The enumeration pin**, `test/released-port-production-spawn.pin.test.ts`. It is a unit-tier vitest test, not a gate script or CI step.
  - It reads every `.ts` file under `packages/cli/test` with the TypeScript AST.
  - A file whose code names the built entry `bin/run.js` may call `reservePort()`/`randomPort()` only as often as its `OUTSIDE_THE_PRODUCTION_COLUMN` entry allows. With no entry, the allowance is zero.
  - "Names" covers both spellings this directory uses (patch round 1). One is a string that ends with the entry: `resolve(HERE, '../bin/run.js')`. The other is the entry spelled as path segments inside one call: `join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'bin', 'run.js')`. For the second, the call's string-literal arguments are split on `/` and read in order, and the entry's segments must all appear among them, in that order.
  - `bin/run.js` is the only entry that can produce a production-posture child: `bin/run-dev.js` sets `NODE_ENV=development` unconditionally before argv is parsed.
  - The ledger holds the four `bin/run.js` files whose every spawn is development posture, each with its reason and its exact draw count.
- **Docblocks.** The `reservePort()` / `randomPort()` docblocks no longer say the race is unclosed. They now say it is closed for the production column, and they name the two uses that may still draw: the development column and instruments.
  - `portContentionError()` now says it is not for a kernel-assigned child. Converted sites stopped calling it, because its "host race, not a verdict" message would hide a real defect there.
  - The stale "the ONLY file in the loud row" count in `boundPortFromBanner()`'s docblock now points at the pin.

## Measured before choosing the mechanism

Built CLI, worktree on `83048c686`. The harness held a port with a live listener for the HELD legs.

| leg | spawn | result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `bin/run.js serve -p HELD` (production) | exit 1, `Port 40349 is already in use` |
| M2 | `bin/run.js serve -p 0` (production) | banner `API:` port 34647, `GET /api/v1/health` on it: 200 |
| M3 | `bin/run.js serve`, `OS_PORT=0` | banner port 43365, health 200 |
| M4 | `bin/run.js serve`, `PORT=0` | banner port 35705, health 200 |
| M5 | `bin/run.js start -p HELD` (production) | exit 1, `Port 40349 is already in use` |
| M6 | `bin/run.js start -p 0` (production) | banner port 33721, health 200 |
| M7 | `bin/run.js serve -p 0 --dev` | banner port 42681, health 200 |
| M8 | `bin/run.js serve -p HELD --dev` | green boot on 40350 (drift) |
| M9 | tsx `run-dev.js serve -p HELD` (the `runServe()` shape) | green boot on HELD+1 (drift) |
| M10 | tsx `run-dev.js start -p HELD` (the `package-install-local-*` shape) | green boot on HELD+1 (drift) |

M9 and M10 confirm that every tsx child is in the development column, including an `os start` whose `serve` child inherits `NODE_ENV=development`.

| `serve-mcp-stdio-early-initialize.integration` | production `serve` + a `--dev` minting boot | both on `KERNEL_ASSIGNED_PORT` |
| `dev-standalone-self-heal.integration` | production `serve` leg + two `os dev` legs through one boot helper | all three on `KERNEL_ASSIGNED_PORT` |

Both compare the bound port with `serve`'s built-in default 3000, and leg 1 also with the held port. Leg 3 already used `holdPort()` |

See the acceptance notes |
| `serve-port-bind-probe.test` | instrument: measures the draw itself, spawns no CLI | draws by design |
| `serve-probe-child-attribution.test` | instrument: `reservePort()` as a port nothing listens on; spawns a driver script, not the CLI | draws by design |

The PM's read was 29 test files calling `portContentionError(`, as the production column. Classified:

- 8 are production posture: the first 8 rows. `start-port-banner-agreement` never called it.
- 3 spawn `bin/run.js --dev`.
- 17 spawn a tsx (development) child, where a lost race drifts instead of exiting.
- 1 is the bind-probe instrument.

## Reverse verification and ablation (one-time, not kept)

Each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode. Every restore ended with blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- **The pin turns red on a reverted site.** In `start-mcp-stdio-early-initialize`, `[CLI, 'start', '-p', KERNEL_ASSIGNED_PORT, …]` was changed to `randomPort()`.
  - Result: `Tests 1 failed | 3 passed (4)`.
  - The failure names the site: `start-mcp-stdio-early-initialize.integration.test.ts: 1 released-port draw(s) (line 287), ledger allows 0`.
- **The lost race, forced (A5), reproduces the hourly-run red deterministically.** The same `os start` leg was spawned on a port the test holds.
  - Result: `AssertionError: initialize was never answered — os start exited 1 before answering — ✗ Port 44877 is already in use.`
  - That is the shape the hourly run recorded on port 45195.
  - On the converted site the child is handed no number, so this hostile condition has nothing to act on. The converted file passes (see Tests).
- **Patch round 1 — the pin sees the segment spelling.**
  - Mutation: a scratch `const SCRATCH_PORT = randomPort();` added beside `published-entry-stderr-error-listener.test.ts`'s `join(PACKAGE_ROOT, 'bin', 'run.js')`. That file names the entry only in segments.
  - Result: `Tests 1 failed | 3 passed (4)` — `published-entry-stderr-error-listener.test.ts: 1 released-port draw(s) (line 82), ledger allows 0`.
  - The first attempt was a no-op: its replacement still contained the anchor text, so the tool refused before running anything. The anchor was changed and the run repeated.
  - Removing the segment reading turns two of the pin's own checks red: the fixture battery (`the built entry spelled in path segments: population: expected false to be true`) and the live-tree check (`published-entry-stderr-error-listener.test.ts spells bin/run.js in segments but is not in the population`).
- **The leg-1 assertion of `start-port-banner-agreement` can fail.** Dropping `--port 0` gives `os start exited 1 before its banner. ✗ Port 38959 is already in use.`: the child took the held `OS_PORT`. Leg 2's counterpart (unset `OS_PORT` ⇒ the child binds 3000) was **not run**, because it would bind 3000 on a container where `PORT=3000` is the shared frontend-debug backend.

- **Reconciled.** `--ran` with exit codes recorded reports `52 derived, 52 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.

## Acceptance notes

- **#24342 carries the development column of #24295's family; #24295 keeps the production column.**
- **The development column still draws, and it goes red on the same race.**
  - That is 31 tsx-entry files plus the 4 ledger files.
  - Measured: M8–M10 above. `serve-port-readback.e2e`'s held-port leg already pins that `runServe()` rejects a drifted boot with `PORT DRIFT`.
  - This PR does not convert them. The card's column is production posture, and the dispatch asked for this reading to be reported, not silently widened. The minting and `os dev` boots converted here sit inside files that also hold a production spawn, through the same boot code.
- **`serve-node-env-production-default`'s fixture `baseUrl` is now a held port, not the server's own port.** Its three legs still split 403 / not-403 on one fixture. The probed Origin is now guaranteed distinct from both the `baseUrl` and the bound port, where it used to be `port + 1`.
- **`check:cli-test-child-env` rule 3 resolves a built-entry child's `NODE_ENV` through exactly one same-file hop.** Splitting that probe into a second function made it red. The spawn stays in the function the `it` blocks call, and a comment there says why.
- **The pin's blind spots are named in its header:**
  - the development column;
  - a production-capable entry spelled some other way — a packed tarball's bin, `dist/` run directly — or with its directory held in a variable before the file name is joined on (`join(BIN_DIR, 'run.js')`);
  - a hand-written released draw that does not call the helper.
